title: Published companion counts do not exclude a majority at half the adopted completeness
abstract: We audit the wide-companion exclusion for main-sequence dust dimmers with published aggregate results. In the independent-detection model, companion fraction f and completeness scale s enter only as their product. We derive lower and upper count-probability bounds from aggregate chance and detection rates. For 91 dimmers with one strict-search detection, half the adopted completeness and f=0.5 give an exact lower-tail probability of at least 0.051855. The one-sided 95% upper endpoint lies between 0.5041 and 0.7030. Thus this count test does not exclude a majority in that sensitivity case. The ten mature field-dwarf dimmers also do not exclude half at adopted completeness: published exact probabilities are 0.08127 and 0.21659. The full sample still excludes a majority at adopted completeness, and excludes companions for every star at half completeness. This is a conditional inference result, with no new observations. We retain the companion-excess null result. The model assumes independent detections, fixed chance rates, a common fraction and a common completeness scale. Code, proof, source aggregate, attribution and checks are included.

display.caption: Count-probability bounds for all 91 dimmers and exact published probabilities for the ten mature field dwarfs. Dashed curves are upper bounds; solid curves are lower bounds.
